incentives.title: Incentives
incentives.standardClass: Standard tax class: no class incentive applies.
incentives.classIncentive: This lot's tax class carries an incentive (see details).

define.tax: The yearly property tax bill, as the County computes it for the latest bill year. A new owner's bill can differ once exemptions drop or the lot is reassessed.
define.value: What the Cook County Assessor says the property is worth: its assessed value divided by the share the law assesses for its class. It sets the tax bill; it is not a sale price.
define.sales: Recorded sales of similar properties near this lot (same tax class), counted only when the County treats them as market sales. The chips say how near and how recent.
define.rent: What renters nearby pay each month, rent plus utilities, from the Census survey of this tract (or a wider area). Not listing prices, and not what a new building would get.
define.incentives: Programs that can help pay for a project in this place: tax-increment money, tax credits and zones with tax breaks. Being inside one means a project can apply, not that it is approved.

program.tif: Tax Increment Financing: a district where growth in property tax pays for public projects and can help private development.
program.oz: A federal Opportunity Zone: investors can defer or cut capital-gains tax by investing here.
program.ez: A State of Illinois Enterprise Zone: sales-tax and other breaks for building and businesses.
program.qct: A HUD Qualified Census Tract: affordable-housing projects here can get a larger federal tax credit.
program.nmtc: A tract eligible for New Markets Tax Credits, a federal credit for investment in low-income areas.

program.forThisLot: What it means for this lot
program.checking: Still checking this program for this lot.
program.notChecked: We couldn't check this program for this lot today, so we can't say whether it applies.

tif.meansIn: This lot is inside the {{name}} TIF district. A project here can ask the City for TIF help (money from the district's fund, often repaid from the new taxes the project creates) until the district ends. Nothing is promised: the City decides project by project.
tif.meansOut: This lot is in no TIF district, so a project here can't get TIF money. Other City programs and grants can still apply.
tif.who: The City's Department of Planning and Development negotiates TIF help; City Council approves each agreement.
tif.source: Source: City of Chicago TIF boundaries and annual reports
tif.reportsChecking: Still checking the district's annual reports.
tif.reportsLate: Couldn't check the district's annual reports in time.
tif.reportsMissing: The district's annual reports didn't come back for this lookup.

oz.meansIn: This lot is in an Opportunity Zone (Census tract {{tract}}). Investors who put capital gains into a project here through a Qualified Opportunity Fund can defer or reduce federal tax on them. It doesn't change the zoning or what can be built.
oz.meansOut: This lot is not in an Opportunity Zone, so investors in a project here get no Opportunity Zone tax benefit.
oz.who: No City approval: investors claim the benefit on their federal taxes through a Qualified Opportunity Fund.
oz.source: Source: US Treasury and HUD Opportunity Zones

ez.meansIn: This lot is in {{name}}. A project here can claim Illinois Enterprise Zone benefits, such as a sales-tax exemption on building materials bought for it.
ez.meansOut: This lot is not in an Enterprise Zone, so there's no Enterprise Zone sales-tax exemption on building materials.
ez.who: Benefits are claimed under State of Illinois rules through the zone's administrator (the City, for Chicago's zones).
ez.source: Source: City of Chicago Enterprise Zone boundaries

qct.meansIn: This lot is in a HUD Qualified Census Tract (tract {{tract}}). An affordable-housing project using Low-Income Housing Tax Credits can count up to 130% of its eligible costs, which means a larger credit. Other kinds of projects aren't affected.
qct.meansOut: This lot is not in a Qualified Census Tract, so an affordable-housing project here gets no automatic credit boost from it.
qct.who: Housing tax credits are awarded in competitions run by the City's Department of Housing and the Illinois Housing Development Authority.

nmtc.meansIn: This lot is in a low-income tract eligible for New Markets Tax Credits (tract {{tract}}). Commercial and community projects here can seek NMTC financing, which often comes on below-market terms.
nmtc.meansOut: This lot is not in an eligible tract, so New Markets Tax Credit financing isn't available here by location.
nmtc.who: Community Development Entities that hold federal allocations choose which projects to finance.

grants.title: City grants in this community area
grants.what: Small Business Improvement Fund grants are paid from TIF money; Neighborhood Opportunity Fund grants come from downtown density fees.

rule.ask: What does {{rule}} mean for a project at {{address}}?

flood.meansIn: FEMA maps this lot in flood zone {{zone}}. Building here has to meet the City's floodplain rules, and a federally backed mortgage on a building in a special flood hazard area needs flood insurance.
flood.meansOut: FEMA maps this lot outside the 100-year floodplain, so the City's floodplain rules don't add requirements here.
flood.who: The City's Department of Buildings applies the floodplain rules on permits; FEMA draws the flood maps.
flood.what: FEMA's flood zones: A and AE are the 100-year floodplain (a 1% chance of flooding each year); X is outside it.
flood.source: Source: FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer (Chicago copy)

landmark.meansIn: This lot is a Chicago Landmark or sits in a landmark district. Permits to alter or demolish a building, add on, or build new here need the Commission on Chicago Landmarks' review and approval.
landmark.meansOut: This lot is not a Chicago Landmark and not in a landmark district, so permits here don't go to the Landmarks Commission.
landmark.who: The Commission on Chicago Landmarks: its staff review most permits, and the Commission hears larger changes.
landmark.what: A building or district the City Council has designated for its history or design; changes to it need the Commission's approval.
landmark.source: Source: City of Chicago landmark maps

historic.meansIn: This lot is in a historic district. A National Register listing on its own doesn't limit what an owner can do with private money, and can open federal and state tax credits for a certified rehabilitation; a Chicago Landmark district also needs the Commission's approval for exterior work.
historic.meansOut: This lot is not in a historic district on the maps we check.
historic.who: National Register: the National Park Service, with Illinois's State Historic Preservation Office. Chicago Landmark districts: the Commission on Chicago Landmarks.
historic.what: An area recognized for its history: on the National Register (federal, honorary with tax credits) or a Chicago Landmark district (City rules apply).
historic.source: Source: City of Chicago historic and National Register district maps

pd.meansIn: This lot is inside a Planned Development. Its own ordinance, not the base district, sets the uses, height and density here, so changing what's allowed means amending that ordinance.
pd.meansOut: This lot is not in a Planned Development, so the base district's rules apply.
pd.who: City Council amends a Planned Development after Plan Commission review; the Zoning Administrator handles minor changes.
pd.what: A site-specific zoning district Council adopts by ordinance for a large or special project; its number points to that ordinance.
pd.source: Source: City of Chicago zoning map

lakefront.meansIn: This lot is in the Lakefront Protection District. Most development here needs a Lakefront Protection review and the Plan Commission's approval.
lakefront.meansOut: This lot is not in the Lakefront Protection District.
lakefront.what: The area along Lake Michigan covered by the Lake Michigan and Chicago Lakefront Protection Ordinance.
lakefront.source: Source: City of Chicago Lakefront Protection District map

tod.meansIn: This lot is near a CTA or Metra station, in a transit-served area: minimum parking can be reduced, and some districts allow more density.
tod.meansOut: This lot is not in a transit-served area, so the usual parking minimums apply.
tod.who: The City's Zoning Administrator applies the reductions on permits; some bonuses need an administrative adjustment or a rezoning.
tod.what: Areas near CTA and Metra stations where Chicago's zoning code relaxes parking and can allow more homes.
tod.source: Source: City of Chicago transit-served location maps

adu.meansIn: Coach houses and basement or attic units can be added to a home here, within the City's ADU rules.
adu.meansOut: Coach houses and conversion units aren't allowed on this lot.
adu.who: The Department of Buildings issues ADU permits; some areas cap how many are approved each year.
adu.what: Accessory dwelling units: a coach house, or a unit in a basement or attic, added to an existing home.
adu.source: Source: City of Chicago ADU area map and zoning code

aro.meansIn: This lot is in an Affordable Requirements Ordinance area, which sets the affordable share for covered projects: generally 10 or more homes that need a zoning change, City land or City money.
aro.meansOut: There's no ARO area on the map we check for this lot. The ordinance can still cover a project here that needs a zoning change or City help.
aro.what: Chicago's Affordable Requirements Ordinance: covered residential projects include affordable homes or, where allowed, pay a fee instead.
aro.source: Source: City of Chicago ARO area map
